rules.title: Foreclosure Fairness Act - Notice and Eviction Protections for Tenants in Foreclosed Properties
rules.requirement: Foreclosure alone is not grounds for eviction; a tenant in a foreclosed property generally keeps their tenancy. If a buyer who wants to personally occupy the property as a primary residence purchases it, the landlord must give the tenant a 90-day notice to quit, and new owners must notify tenants in English and Spanish that they are not required to move.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential rental units in properties that have been foreclosed upon; notice posting method varies by building size (10 or fewer units vs. more than 10 units).
rules.exemptions: Month-to-month tenants and two- and three-family owner-occupied units are NOT exempt from the 90-day notice requirement (i.e., no exemption applies to them).
rules.quoted_span: Before a tenant can be evicted due to foreclosure, the landlord must provide the tenant with a 90 -day notice to qui t when the foreclosed property has been purchased by a buyer who wants to personally occupy it as his or her primary residence.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the new owner/purchaser intends to personally occupy the unit as a primary residence, and total number of dwelling units in the building (affects notice posting method)

rules.conflict_note: Separate, more detailed notice procedures and posting requirements are set out at N.J.S.A. 2A:50-70(c)2 for buildings with more than 10 units, and pressure-tactic prohibitions at N.J.S.A. 2A:50-71(b); these are part of the same Foreclosure Fairness Act scheme.

rules.title: Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Act
rules.requirement: Eligible senior citizens, permanently disabled tenants, or qualifying disabled veterans living in a building being converted to a condominium, cooperative, or fee-simple ownership may be protected from eviction for up to 40 years, provided their family income does not exceed a set threshold.
rules.key_value: Up to 40 years of eviction protection; income cap = 3x county average per-person income or $50,000, whichever is greater
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to buildings undergoing condominium, cooperative, or fee-simple conversion where qualifying tenants (62+, permanently disabled, or qualifying disabled veteran) have resided at least one year prior to the conversion recording date and meet an income threshold.
rules.quoted_span: Tenants may be protected from eviction for 40 years if their family income is not more than three (3) times the average per person income in their county or $50,000.00, whichever  is greater (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.28).

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the building is undergoing condominium/cooperative/fee-simple conversion, and whether the tenant qualifies by age, disability, veteran status, tenancy duration, and income

rules.conflict_note: An amendment (Tenant Protection Act of 1992) extends similar protections to additional tenants in Hudson County who did not otherwise qualify, but the text does not attribute this to a specific city, so it is not separately recorded.
